_comment: Registry of research modules shown in 'Research log'. Add one entry per assignment once its files have been inspected and validated. Never add an entry for work that does not exist yet.

sources.name: Gross Rent as a Percentage of Household Income in the Past 12 Months
sources.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey
sources.used_for: Rent burden and severe rent burden rates; renter household counts

sources.name: Median Household Income in the Past 12 Months (in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars)
sources.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey
sources.used_for: Median household income by ZIP; income-based pressure index

sources.name: Affordable Housing Production by Building
sources.publisher: NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD), NYC Open Data
sources.geography: Building records with borough and postcode
sources.universe: Buildings in projects counted toward the City's affordable housing plans
sources.used_for: Counted affordable units (new construction and preservation) by ZIP and borough

sources.name: 2020 Cartographic Boundary File, ZCTA5, 1:500,000
sources.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau (retrieved with the R package tigris)

modules.title: Assignment Three — Rent Burden (Brooklyn)
modules.notes: Brooklyn-only analysis with a policy memo. Used an earlier HPD download (accessed 2026-09-26 per the assignment's source log).
modules.integration: Used as an independent cross-check: all 38 Brooklyn ZCTAs reproduce HW3's rent-burdened and valid-renter counts exactly. Its HPD figures are not shown because they come from an older download.

modules.title: Homework 4 — Rent Burden in New York City
modules.scope: 185 ZCTAs across the five boroughs (179 with computable rates)
modules.notes: Citywide extension: borough comparison, ZIP comparison, rent burden vs. HPD activity, income vs. rent burden, and two rank-based affordability pressure indices.
modules.integration: Primary basis of this site. Every figure is recomputed from the raw files by pipeline/build_data.R using the same logic as rent_burden_nyc_analysis.Rmd.

modules.title: Portfolio extension — policy simulator, policy context and About page
modules.scope: Builds on the HW4 data; no new datasets
modules.notes: Added after feedback from the course professor: a what-if simulator that recomputes the HW4 pressure index under hypothetical increases in affordable housing activity, a structured policy-context section, and a standalone About page.
modules.integration: The simulator reuses the published HW4 counts and formula, checks on load that it reproduces the published index, and was cross-checked against an independent R implementation (validation/simulation_crosscheck.md). It is labelled as an illustrative simulation, not a causal forecast.
